Analyzing the image carefully:

**Affected plant part:** Whole banana plant — leaf and stem/pseudostem area visible.

**Key visual features observed:**
- The banana plant shows a large, mostly green leaf in the foreground
- Visible yellowing on parts of the plant, particularly on surrounding/older leaves
- The plant structure appears somewhat intact but stressed
- Ground debris and surrounding vegetation are visible, consistent with a field setting
- The yellowing appears progressive — older leaves showing more color change while the newer central leaf remains greener

**Reasoning through the classes:**
- **Anthracnose:** Typically produces dark, sunken lesions on fruit — no obvious fruit lesions visible
- **Bunchy_Top:** Would show stunted, bunched leaves with dark green streaks — plant appears more normal in structure
- **Cigar_End_Rot:** Affects fruit tips specifically — no rotting fruit tips visible
- **Cordana_Leaf_Spot:** Produces distinct oval brown spots with yellow halos on leaf surfaces — no clearly defined spots with halos visible
- **Panama_Disease (Fusarium wilt):** Causes progressive yellowing starting from outer/older leaves working inward, eventual leaf collapse; the pattern of a still-green younger leaf surrounded by yellowing older foliage fits well
- **Yellow_And_Black_Sigatoka:** Causes yellow-to-black streaks/lesions on leaves — no distinct black streaking pattern is evident

The progressive yellowing from outer leaves inward, with the central/newer leaf retaining green color, strongly matches the classic presentation of **Panama Disease** (Fusarium oxysporum wilt).
